objects.name: EKC attack-pattern properties
objects.description: Top-level properties carrying the EKC sub-technique ID, stage, version added, and detection signals.

objects.name: Keep a model bill of materials (M-BOM) for every deployed model, including base model identity, fine-tuning data...
objects.description: Keep a model bill of materials (M-BOM) for every deployed model, including base model identity, fine-tuning data hashes, and adapter provenance.

objects.name: Sign and verify model artifacts. Pin specific commit hashes for registry-hosted models.
objects.description: Sign and verify model artifacts. Pin specific commit hashes for registry-hosted models.

objects.name: Quarantine and sandbox newly added MCP servers. Review tool descriptions as untrusted input.
objects.description: Quarantine and sandbox newly added MCP servers. Review tool descriptions as untrusted input.

objects.name: Routine backdoor-trigger scanning against deployed models using published benchmarks.
objects.description: Routine backdoor-trigger scanning against deployed models using published benchmarks.

objects.name: EKC-0.1: Training data poisoning
objects.description: Inject manipulated examples into a public dataset, web-scraped corpus, or labeling pipeline that future training runs will ingest.

objects.name: EKC-0.2: Fine-tuning backdoor
objects.description: Distribute a fine-tuning adapter, LoRA, or full-model checkpoint with a hidden trigger-and-behavior pair.

objects.name: EKC-0.3: Pre-trained model trojan
objects.description: Publish a malicious model to a public registry (Hugging Face, Ollama Library, GitHub) under a plausible name or by typosquatting a real one.

objects.name: EKC-0.4: Tokenizer or preprocessing manipulation
objects.description: Alter tokenization, normalization, or feature-extraction code in an upstream dependency to add a covert input channel.

objects.name: EKC-0.5: Malicious MCP server or tool catalog entry
objects.description: Publish a tool description, MCP server manifest, or function definition designed to be invoked by downstream agents and exploit them through prompt injection in the tool description itself.

objects.name: Rate-limit and behavior-cluster prompt traffic per user identity.
objects.description: Rate-limit and behavior-cluster prompt traffic per user identity.

objects.name: Redact identifying response artifacts.
objects.description: Redact identifying response artifacts.

objects.name: Add canary tokens to the system prompt that fire on exfiltration.
objects.description: Add canary tokens to the system prompt that fire on exfiltration.

objects.name: Restrict tool enumeration to authenticated, audited callers.
objects.description: Restrict tool enumeration to authenticated, audited callers.

objects.name: EKC-1.1: Model fingerprinting
objects.description: Identify the base model, fine-tune family, and version of a deployed LLM through response-style probing, latency analysis, or known-answer tests.

objects.name: EKC-1.2: System prompt enumeration
objects.description: Use leakage queries, role-play probes, or boundary-case prompts to recover the system prompt or its main constraints.

objects.name: EKC-1.3: Capability and tool enumeration
objects.description: Discover which tools, plugins, MCP servers, or function-call interfaces the agent has access to.

objects.name: EKC-1.4: Guardrail mapping
objects.description: Map the policy boundary by probing refusal patterns and finding topics, formats, or input shapes that bypass classifiers.

objects.name: EKC-1.5: Embedding and retrieval surface discovery
objects.description: Identify which retrieval sources the system reads from (vector store contents, document corpora, web fetch domains).

objects.name: EKC-1.6: Peer agent and Agent Card enumeration
objects.description: Enumerate the remote agents a target agent can delegate to, and the skills, endpoints, auth schemes and extended capabilities those agents advertise. In A2A deployments the public Agent Card sits at a well-known path and an authenticated extended card can expose more. The output is a map of which peer the attacker should impersonate, poison, or route through.
x_ekc_detection_signals: Bulk or sequential requests for /.well-known/agent-card.json across many hosts from one source.
Extended Agent Card requests from identities that never send tasks afterwards.
Agent Card fetches for internal agents from outside the network ranges that normally call them.

objects.name: Keep the public Agent Card to what an unauthenticated caller needs. Put additional skills in the extended card,...
objects.description: Keep the public Agent Card to what an unauthenticated caller needs. Put additional skills in the extended card, which A2A v1.0 says must require authentication, and keep internal service URLs and credentials out of both cards, as the specification advises.

objects.name: Return extended-card content per caller. The specification requires agents to check a client's permissions before...
objects.description: Return extended-card content per caller. The specification requires agents to check a client's permissions before returning privileged information.

objects.name: Rate-limit and log card retrieval like any other discovery endpoint.
objects.description: Rate-limit and log card retrieval like any other discovery endpoint.

objects.name: Indirect-injection detection on every untrusted inbound content stream: web, email, RAG corpus, MCP tool...
objects.description: Indirect-injection detection on every untrusted inbound content stream: web, email, RAG corpus, MCP tool descriptions, multi-modal inputs.

objects.name: EKC-2.1: Adversarial prompt crafting
objects.description: Build a prompt-injection payload tailored to the fingerprinted target model, guardrails, and toolset from Stage 1.

objects.name: EKC-2.2: Multi-modal payload construction
objects.description: Embed instructions in images, audio, PDFs, or structured documents that a multi-modal model will parse.

objects.name: EKC-2.3: Malicious tool or MCP package
objects.description: Build a tool that looks benign in name and description but executes attacker-controlled actions when invoked.

objects.name: EKC-2.4: Jailbreak chain assembly
objects.description: Combine known bypass techniques (persona priming, encoding tricks, low-resource language pivots, structured role-play) into a single payload that defeats layered guardrails.

objects.name: EKC-2.5: AI-generated polymorphic malware
objects.description: Use a model to produce semantically equivalent but lexically diverse malware variants that evade signature-based detection.

objects.name: EKC-3.1: Indirect prompt injection via web content
objects.description: A browsing or web-fetching agent retrieves an attacker-controlled page with instructions in it.

objects.name: EKC-3.2: RAG corpus poisoning
objects.description: An attacker submits content (via support tickets, public docs, code contributions, or vector-store ingestion) that will later be retrieved as context for an LLM.

objects.name: EKC-3.3: Email or message-borne injection
objects.description: Instructions placed in an email that an AI assistant is configured to read or summarize.

objects.name: EKC-3.4: Document-borne injection
objects.description: Instructions placed in PDFs, spreadsheets, or office documents processed by an AI workflow.

objects.name: EKC-3.5: Tool-description poisoning
objects.description: Instructions placed in the descriptions or schemas of MCP tools or function definitions exposed to the agent.

objects.name: EKC-3.6: Image, audio, or QR-code injection
objects.description: Instructions encoded in non-text modalities that a multi-modal agent will process.

objects.name: EKC-3.7: Crafted assistant link delivery
objects.description: Deliver a payload as a link that opens an AI assistant with an attacker-written prompt already filled in (for example through a ?q= or ?prompt= URL parameter), often behind a "Summarize with AI" button or in an email. One click replaces the user's own prompt with the attacker's. When the prompt tells the assistant to remember a source as trusted, the delivery doubles as a memory write.
x_ekc_detection_signals: URLs pointing at assistant domains whose prompt parameter contains memory or trust language ("remember", "trusted source", "in future conversations", "authoritative").
The same prefilled-prompt template showing up across inbound email from unrelated senders.
A memory write in the assistant within seconds of the user opening such a link.

objects.name: Hunt for prefilled-prompt links in mail, chat and proxy logs. Microsoft published starter queries for this in...
objects.description: Hunt for prefilled-prompt links in mail, chat and proxy logs. Microsoft published starter queries for this in February 2026.

objects.name: Require explicit user confirmation before a prompt that arrived through a URL can write to memory.
objects.description: Require explicit user confirmation before a prompt that arrived through a URL can write to memory.

objects.name: Show users what was saved to memory and give them a one-step way to remove it.
objects.description: Show users what was saved to memory and give them a one-step way to remove it.

objects.name: EKC-3.8: Malicious or impersonated peer agent
objects.description: Get the payload in front of the target agent through an agent it delegates work to. The attacker runs a remote agent, or advertises one with a spoofed or tampered Agent Card, so that the target routes tasks to it. Every response that comes back is model-readable content the client agent will reason over. The protocol carries the payload faithfully; the weakness is the trust the client places in the peer.
x_ekc_detection_signals: Delegation to an agent whose Agent Card is unsigned, whose signature fails, or whose signing key changed without notice.
A newly registered peer agent with a name or description close to an existing internal agent.
Peer agent responses that contain imperative instructions aimed at the client agent rather than task results.

objects.name: Verify Agent Card signatures (A2A v1.0 defines JWS signatures over a JCS-canonicalized card) and pin keys for known...
objects.description: Verify Agent Card signatures (A2A v1.0 defines JWS signatures over a JCS-canonicalized card) and pin keys for known peers.

objects.name: Keep an allowlist of peer agents per workflow. Treat discovery of a new peer as a change that needs review.
objects.description: Keep an allowlist of peer agents per workflow. Treat discovery of a new peer as a change that needs review.

objects.name: Handle every peer response as untrusted input, the same way the framework treats retrieved web content.
objects.description: Handle every peer response as untrusted input, the same way the framework treats retrieved web content.

objects.name: EKC-3.9: Interface-layer injection against computer-use agents
objects.description: Place instructions where a computer-use or browser agent will see them on screen: fake error dialogs, "verify you are human" prompts, ClickFix-style copy-and-run steps, calendar invites, or pages served only to AI user agents. The payload targets what the agent perceives (rendered pixels, accessibility tree, DOM text) rather than a text field a filter would scan.
x_ekc_detection_signals: Pages that return different content when the user agent identifies as an AI browser or agent.
On-screen text in agent sessions that asks for clipboard, terminal or Run-dialog actions.
Calendar invites or documents with hidden or zero-size text processed by a browsing agent.

objects.name: Run computer-use agents in an isolated VM or container with no access to the user's real profile, files or password...
objects.description: Run computer-use agents in an isolated VM or container with no access to the user's real profile, files or password manager.

objects.name: Strip or flag instruction-like text in rendered content before the agent plans its next action.
objects.description: Strip or flag instruction-like text in rendered content before the agent plans its next action.

objects.name: Block clipboard-to-terminal and Run-dialog sequences initiated by the agent.
objects.description: Block clipboard-to-terminal and Run-dialog sequences initiated by the agent.

objects.name: Tool-call argument lineage tracking. Any tool invocation whose arguments derive from untrusted text is treated as...
objects.description: Tool-call argument lineage tracking. Any tool invocation whose arguments derive from untrusted text is treated as high-risk by default.

objects.name: EKC-4.1: Direct prompt injection success
objects.description: The user-facing prompt achieves the attacker's policy violation.

objects.name: EKC-4.2: Indirect prompt injection success
objects.description: Instructions delivered via Stage 3 are followed by the model when the content is processed.

objects.name: EKC-4.3: Confused-deputy tool invocation
objects.description: The model invokes a privileged tool on behalf of the attacker, using the agent's own permissions.

objects.name: EKC-4.4: Guardrail or classifier bypass
objects.description: A safety classifier or rule-based filter is evaded such that disallowed content is produced or disallowed actions are taken.

objects.name: EKC-4.5: Memory or context pollution
objects.description: A persistent memory store is updated with attacker-controlled content that will influence future sessions.

objects.name: EKC-4.6: Computer-use action hijack
objects.description: The computer-use or browser agent carries out the attacker's steps as GUI and OS actions: clicking, typing, opening file:// paths, running shell commands, or driving a password manager integration it was granted for user tasks. No tool API is misused. The agent operates the machine the way the user would, so the actions look like ordinary user activity to the endpoint.
x_ekc_detection_signals: Browser agents navigating to file:// URIs or local network addresses that the user's task did not reference.
Shell or terminal processes spawned with the agent as the parent process.
Password manager item reads during an agent session that were not part of the stated task.

objects.name: Deny file:// and local-network navigation to agents by default.
objects.description: Deny file:// and local-network navigation to agents by default.

objects.name: Require out-of-band human confirmation for credential retrieval, downloads and command execution.
objects.description: Require out-of-band human confirmation for credential retrieval, downloads and command execution.

objects.name: Record agent sessions (screens plus action log) so an investigator can replay what the agent saw.
objects.description: Record agent sessions (screens plus action log) so an investigator can replay what the agent saw.

objects.name: Memory write audit trails.
objects.description: Memory write audit trails.

objects.name: Change control on system prompts and stored skills.
objects.description: Change control on system prompts and stored skills.

objects.name: Attestation on MCP endpoints.
objects.description: Attestation on MCP endpoints.

objects.name: EKC-5.1: Persistent memory implant
objects.description: Inject content into long-term memory, user preference stores, or per-account context that will be reloaded in future sessions.

objects.name: EKC-5.2: System prompt override
objects.description: Modify a custom GPT, assistant configuration, or agent definition to embed attacker instructions in its system prompt.

objects.name: EKC-5.3: Malicious connector installation
objects.description: Cause a user or admin to install an attacker-controlled MCP server, plugin, or browser extension that gives the attacker a persistent foothold.

objects.name: EKC-5.4: RAG corpus persistence
objects.description: Ensure poisoned documents stay in the vector store across re-indexing operations.

objects.name: EKC-5.5: Stored skill or workflow contamination
objects.description: Modify a stored skill, automation, or saved workflow that the agent will load and execute on a schedule or on demand.

objects.name: EKC-5.6: Shared agent memory poisoning
objects.description: Poison a memory store that more than one principal reads: team or organization memory, a knowledge base agents write back into, a shared scratchpad in a multi-agent system, or consolidated summaries that replace raw history. EKC-5.1 compromises one user's future sessions. This variant compromises every agent and user that reads the shared store, and the poisoned entry is often rewritten by summarization so it no longer looks like the original payload.
x_ekc_detection_signals: Writes to shared memory whose content traces back to untrusted retrieved content or a peer agent.
A single memory entry that suddenly appears in the context of many unrelated users or agents.
Summarization or consolidation jobs that introduce imperative instructions not present in any source turn.

objects.name: Attach provenance (writer identity, source content hash, time) to every memory entry and keep it through summarization.
objects.description: Attach provenance (writer identity, source content hash, time) to every memory entry and keep it through summarization.

objects.name: Separate per-user memory from shared memory. Require review or a higher trust level to write to the shared store.
objects.description: Separate per-user memory from shared memory. Require review or a higher trust level to write to the shared store.

objects.name: Support point-in-time rollback of memory, the same way a corpus or database is restored after tampering.
objects.description: Support point-in-time rollback of memory, the same way a corpus or database is restored after tampering.

objects.name: Conversation-graph analysis to surface recurring instruction sources.
objects.description: Conversation-graph analysis to surface recurring instruction sources.

objects.name: Entropy analysis on agent-to-agent fields.
objects.description: Entropy analysis on agent-to-agent fields.

objects.name: EKC-6.1: LLM channel as C2
objects.description: Encode commands in seemingly benign user prompts, retrieved documents, or tool outputs that the agent reads on a schedule.

objects.name: EKC-6.2: Memory-mediated C2
objects.description: Use the agent's long-term memory store as a dead-drop. The attacker writes instructions to memory through one entry point, the agent acts on them through another.

objects.name: EKC-6.3: RAG-mediated C2
objects.description: Update a poisoned document in the vector store to deliver new instructions. The agent retrieves them on the next relevant query.

objects.name: EKC-6.4: Tool-output C2
objects.description: A compromised MCP server returns instruction-laden responses on each invocation, steering the agent's subsequent behavior.

objects.name: EKC-6.5: Cross-session steganographic C2
objects.description: Encode command payloads in fields the agent passes between sessions (user notes, project descriptions, ticket comments) where they evade content classification because each fragment looks innocuous on its own.

objects.name: EKC-6.6: Inter-agent session smuggling
objects.description: A malicious remote agent uses an open, stateful agent-to-agent session to slip extra instructions into the exchange between the client's request and its own final answer. Because the session persists across turns, the remote agent can adapt its instructions to what the client reveals. The user sees only the client's final summary. Unit 42 demonstrated system-prompt leakage and an unauthorized trade this way over A2A.
x_ekc_detection_signals: Remote-agent turns that ask the client for its instructions, tool schemas or conversation history.
Tool invocations by the client agent that occur mid-delegation and are absent from the user's request.
Long multi-turn delegations where the turn count is out of line with the task type.

objects.name: Ground the session in the user's original intent and end delegations that drift off-task.
objects.description: Ground the session in the user's original intent and end delegations that drift off-task.

objects.name: Require out-of-band human approval for sensitive tools invoked while a delegation is open.
objects.description: Require out-of-band human approval for sensitive tools invoked while a delegation is open.

objects.name: Surface remote-agent turns and resulting tool calls to the user instead of only the final consolidated answer.
objects.description: Surface remote-agent turns and resulting tool calls to the user instead of only the final consolidated answer.

objects.description: Classical DLP, monitoring, segmentation.

objects.name: EKC-7a: Classical data exfiltration
objects.description: Sensitive data is exfiltrated, systems are impaired, or fraud is committed through the compromised AI system or by AI-scaled classical means.

objects.name: Query-pattern analytics.
objects.description: Query-pattern analytics.

objects.name: Memorization probes in red-team suites.
objects.description: Memorization probes in red-team suites.

objects.name: Watermarking of model outputs.
objects.description: Watermarking of model outputs.

objects.name: EKC-7b.1: API-based model extraction
objects.description: Reconstruct an approximation of a deployed model's weights or decision boundary by querying it at scale and training a surrogate.

objects.name: EKC-7b.2: Training-data extraction
objects.description: Recover verbatim or near-verbatim training examples, including sensitive PII or proprietary content, through memorization-targeting prompts.

objects.name: EKC-7b.3: Membership inference
objects.description: Determine whether a specific record was in the training set. Has downstream implications for privacy regulation and confidentiality.

objects.name: EKC-7b.4: System prompt and instruction extraction
objects.description: Recover proprietary system prompts that encode business logic, pricing rules, or competitive positioning.

objects.name: EKC-7b.5: Capability mining
objects.description: Use the deployed model to perform tasks the attacker's own infrastructure cannot. The access becomes a capability transfer.

objects.name: Per-tool blast-radius limits.
objects.description: Per-tool blast-radius limits.

objects.name: Human-in-the-loop on high-impact tools.
objects.description: Human-in-the-loop on high-impact tools.

objects.name: Identity propagation review: does the downstream system know it is acting on behalf of an agent, not a user?
objects.description: Identity propagation review: does the downstream system know it is acting on behalf of an agent, not a user?

objects.name: EKC-7c.1: Tool-mediated lateral action
objects.description: The agent invokes legitimate tools (email send, file write, ticket creation, payment authorization) on behalf of the attacker.

objects.name: EKC-7c.2: Cross-app pivot
objects.description: The agent moves from one connected application to another (calendar to CRM to payment processor) by chaining tool calls.

objects.name: EKC-7c.3: Identity confusion attack
objects.description: The agent acts in a context where downstream systems treat its actions as the actions of a privileged user, granting privileges the attacker does not directly hold.

objects.name: EKC-7c.4: Recursive agent abuse
objects.description: A compromised agent invokes other agents, propagating the compromise across an agent fabric without classical lateral movement.

objects.name: EKC-7c.5: Workflow weaponization
objects.description: A stored automation or scheduled workflow runs the attacker's intended action on a recurring basis.

objects.name: EKC-7c.6: Agent credential and token theft
objects.description: Lift the credentials an agent holds or brokers (OAuth access and refresh tokens, MCP server tokens, API keys, session cookies, CI secrets) so the attacker can use them outside the agent. Paths include steering the agent to read its own environment or config files, abusing token passthrough or over-broad scopes in an MCP proxy, and malicious MCP servers that collect forwarded tokens. Once the token leaves, the attacker no longer needs the agent.
x_ekc_detection_signals: Agent file reads of /proc/*/environ, credential stores, or agent config files such as mcp.json.
Use of an agent-issued token from an IP, ASN or user agent the agent never runs from.
MCP servers receiving tokens whose audience is not the server itself (token passthrough).

objects.name: Follow the MCP authorization rules: servers must not accept tokens not issued to them, and proxies need per-client...
objects.description: Follow the MCP authorization rules: servers must not accept tokens not issued to them, and proxies need per-client consent.

objects.name: Issue short-lived, narrowly scoped tokens per agent and per task. Bind them to the workload where the IdP supports it.
objects.description: Issue short-lived, narrowly scoped tokens per agent and per task. Bind them to the workload where the IdP supports it.

objects.name: Apply Meta's "Agents Rule of Two": no single agent should process untrusted input, hold secrets or private data, and...
objects.description: Apply Meta's "Agents Rule of Two": no single agent should process untrusted input, hold secrets or private data, and change state or communicate externally at the same time.
